reports.note: Actual Game.tick, normal bullets/HP/AI/offered upgrades, explicit dense spawn isolation. Legacy bullet baseline is used only when legacyBulletComparison=true; otherwise both passes retain default bullet rules and onPass controls the renderer experiment. One fixed1/60 tick per render; raf mode waits before every render, batch8 keeps historical eight-render yields. This is a paced fixed-workload comparison: no product-loop catch-up, interpolation, HUD, audio or persistence. Render time is game.time for deterministic camera/shake. Call wall times include instrumentation; combined includes event draining and render. rAF callback intervals include browser scheduling and are not presented FPS or actual GPU execution. QA data stays in memory.

note: Explicit in-memory8851 QA. Each A/B/A arm uses a newly constructed original256 NPC rig/context and the same locally loaded model; candidate calls compileAsync with the actual SkinnedMesh/unlit MeshBasic materials before the first draw. GLB load is completed in all arms before preparation and excluded from preparation/combat clocks. This is a fresh renderer context comparison, not hardware/driver-cold proof. Preparation, first native render and whole fixed1/60 batch8 combat are separate. Shader API-ready alone does not verify link success, uniform/geometry/VAO/bone/texture upload or first draw/read latency. No product catch-up/HUD/audio/save/FPS/GPU-execution or real-memory claim. Normal game rules/state/events are compared; source pose/geometry/UV/texture/material expression and public renderer state are checked before/after prep, while legitimate material version/program caches are recorded. Product load/preload remains unchanged; candidate is QA-only.
